name: Physaria

project_scope.selection_mode: Five canonical species, formerly listed in Master Plant Pool as Lesquerella
project_scope.source_pool_separate_concept: Lesquerella grandiflora is accepted as Paysonia grandiflora, NOT Physaria grandiflora; separate installer/taxonomy dependency; do not install or fold into Physaria.
project_scope.range_note: All five canonical species retain existing provisional range metadata. No range decision changed.

shared_genus_recognition.look_here_first: FIRST inspect a mature fruit: a short silicle with two valves and a replum, then its stalk (pedicel), the valve surfaces and the plant's hairs. Under a 10–30× lens check whether hairs are stellate and asymmetrically notched. Record basal versus stem-leaf shapes and annual taproot versus perennial caudex.
shared_traits: Brassicaceae herbs with four sepals and usually four yellow-to-orange petals, typically six tetradynamous stamens; flower color is not a reliable species split.
Leaves basal and on stems; hairs often stellate or stellate-scalelike, requiring magnification for ray/notch characters.
Short many-seeded silicles; inspect valve surface, replum and fruiting-pedicel posture. Not every Physaria fruit is strongly inflated.
The five canonical species are historical Lesquerella sensu lato names now treated under Physaria.
shared_genus_recognition.memory_cue: Flower says mustard; fruit stalk, valve interior and star-shaped hairs say which bladderpod.

species_comparison_matrix.densiflora: Annual or biennial, fine taproot; low, compact
species_comparison_matrix.sessilis: Annual/biennial branch of FNA key; verify root/base on specimen
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Whole plant with exposed root or caudex; avoid uprooting sensitive plants

species_comparison_matrix.densiflora: Basal leaves often lobed; upper leaves shorter and narrower
species_comparison_matrix.engelmannii: Dense stellate-hairy leaves; compare basal and cauline blades
species_comparison_matrix.gracilis: Basal oblanceolate/obovate; stem leaves narrower, often sessile
species_comparison_matrix.recurvata: Basal obovate/rhombic; distal stem leaves sessile
species_comparison_matrix.sessilis: Upper leaves sessile; not diagnostic alone because several others also have sessile upper leaves
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Matched basal and upper-stem leaf attachments with scale

species_comparison_matrix.densiflora: Straight to slightly curved, spreading to near-horizontal
species_comparison_matrix.engelmannii: Short, ascending on dense racemes (canonical provisional cue)
species_comparison_matrix.gracilis: Straight or slightly curved; fruits elevated on short gynophore
species_comparison_matrix.recurvata: Recurved backward at maturity, fruit may become downturned
species_comparison_matrix.sessilis: Not a sole validated separator; record mature pedicel posture for review
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Side-on full fruiting raceme with mature stalks visible

species_comparison_matrix.densiflora: No diagnostic gynophore length established in current card
species_comparison_matrix.engelmannii: No diagnostic gynophore length established in current card
species_comparison_matrix.gracilis: Distinct gynophore 1–2 mm between pedicel and fruit (FNA key)
species_comparison_matrix.recurvata: No 1–2 mm gynophore claim; rely first on recurved pedicel
species_comparison_matrix.sessilis: Fruit attachment requires direct macro verification
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Millimeter macro of pedicel–fruit junction, especially P. gracilis

species_comparison_matrix.densiflora: Smooth exterior and glabrous interior in FNA annual key
species_comparison_matrix.engelmannii: Fruit-valve surface requires paired verified macro
species_comparison_matrix.gracilis: Glabrous fruit valves in FNA annual key
species_comparison_matrix.recurvata: Glabrous fruit valves in FNA description
species_comparison_matrix.sessilis: Exterior papillose; INSIDE densely pubescent (strong FNA separator)
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: One intact and one opened ripe fruit per species; label outer/inner valve

species_comparison_matrix.densiflora: Dense appressed stellate/scalelike hairs; FNA describes U-shaped notch on one side
species_comparison_matrix.engelmannii: Asymmetric stellate hairs with a deep notch on one side (FNA perennial key)
species_comparison_matrix.gracilis: Pubescent; diagnostic notch form not verified here
species_comparison_matrix.recurvata: Sparse stellate 3–6-rayed hairs in FNA treatment
species_comparison_matrix.sessilis: Stellate hair details need direct verification
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Same-magnification 10–30× abaxial leaf hairs with ray/notch arrows

species_comparison_matrix.gracilis: Dense flower clusters but open/wiry branched overall plant
species_comparison_matrix.recurvata: Loose racemes in FNA species treatment
species_comparison_matrix.sessilis: Do not infer from compactness alone
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Matched flowering and fruiting racemes with stem length in frame

species_comparison_matrix.densiflora: Annual + straight/spreading fruit stalk + asymmetric notched hairs
species_comparison_matrix.engelmannii: Perennial caudex + deeply notched stellate hairs
species_comparison_matrix.gracilis: Annual + 1–2 mm gynophore + straight/slightly curved pedicel
species_comparison_matrix.sessilis: Papillose outer valve + densely hairy INNER valve
species_comparison_matrix.photo_role: Paired fruit and trichome macros for each species

species_field_paths.look: Check the annual taproot, then straight-to-spreading fruit stalk and notched stellate hairs.
species_field_paths.confirm: FNA annual key: smooth exterior, glabrous inner valve; pedicel straight or slightly curved.
species_field_paths.caution: Low habit, yellow flowers and sessile upper leaves overlap other species.

species_field_paths.look: Find a perennial base/caudex, then examine an asymmetric deeply notched stellate hair.
species_field_paths.confirm: FNA perennial key identifies a deep unilateral trichome notch; compact dense raceme supports but does not prove.
species_field_paths.caution: Annual P. densiflora also has asymmetrically notched hairs: inspect the root/caudex.

species_field_paths.look: Look at the junction immediately beneath a ripe fruit: a short gynophore about 1–2 mm.
species_field_paths.confirm: Straight to slightly curved fruiting pedicel; delicate annual stems.
species_field_paths.caution: A sessile upper leaf is common in other taxa and does not diagnose this species.

species_field_paths.look: Follow the mature fruiting pedicel: it curves backward (recurves).
species_field_paths.confirm: Loose raceme; FNA describes annual/biennial taproot and 3–6-rayed stellate hairs.
species_field_paths.caution: Immature stalks may not yet be recurved; check several ripe fruits.

species_field_paths.look: Open a mature silicle: outer valve papillose, inner valve densely hairy.
species_field_paths.confirm: Compare both surfaces at high magnification; use sessile upper leaves only as a supporting character.
species_field_paths.caution: The epithet sessilis is a memory cue, not a stand-alone ID: P. gracilis and P. recurvata may also have sessile distal leaves.

overlap_cautions: This is a teaching framework from canonical provisional cards plus Flora of North America, not a certified dichotomous key. Examine mature fruits and 10–30× hairs for difficult identifications.
Yellow four-petaled flowers, stellate pubescence and inflated-looking fruits overlap widely; never identify solely by these.
P. densiflora and P. engelmannii both have asymmetrically notched trichomes; life history and caudex/taproot separate their FNA key paths.
The upper-leaf 'sessilis' cue is not exclusive. The stronger P. sessilis separator is papillose exterior and densely hairy inner valve.
P. recurvata's pedicel posture develops with maturity; immature racemes may mislead.
The Master Plant Pool still spells the six source names as Lesquerella; five map to canonical Physaria and L. grandiflora maps to Paysonia grandiflora. Do not count all six as Physaria.

local_lookalikes.name: Paysonia grandiflora (source-pool Lesquerella grandiflora)
local_lookalikes.compare: Separate accepted genus; historical name appears alongside five Physaria names. Require Paysonia-specific fruit/leaf diagnostics; do not treat as a sixth Physaria.

local_lookalikes.name: Physaria lindheimeri
local_lookalikes.compare: FNA annual key: sigmoid/horizontal/recurved fruiting pedicels and trichomes lacking P. densiflora's U-shaped notch; comparison only unless installed.

local_lookalikes.name: Other yellow-flowered Brassicaceae (Draba, Lepidium, etc.)
local_lookalikes.compare: Confirm mature silicle valve architecture, replum and stellate trichomes rather than relying on flower color.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: ALL FIVE: paired whole-plant view with basal rosette, stem and intact base (annual taproot versus perennial caudex); label life-history evidence.
ALL FIVE: matched flowering and mature fruiting racemes, photographed side-on with centimeter scale; label pedicel angle.
P. densiflora versus P. engelmannii: matched 10–30× abaxial stellate hairs showing unilateral U/deep notch AND root/caudex.
P. gracilis: 1–2 mm gynophore between fruit and pedicel with millimeter ruler and annotation.
P. recurvata: mature recurved fruiting stalks from several fruits in same inflorescence; compare immature stalks.
P. sessilis: opened mature silicle showing dense INSIDE hairs, plus exterior papillose surface at equal magnification.
P. densiflora: opened ripe fruit with smooth exterior and glabrous interior, matched to P. sessilis.
ALL FIVE: upper-leaf attachment and basal/cauline blade comparison to demonstrate why sessile leaves are not exclusive.
Physaria versus Paysonia grandiflora: only after diagnostic review, matched fruit macro explaining accepted-genus distinction.
